event: Born Victor-Marie Hugo in Besançon, France.
Writes in his diary that he will be 'Chateaubriand or nothing'.
Co-founds the periodical Le Conservateur littéraire with his brothers.
Publishes Odes et poésies diverses and marries Adèle Foucher.
Publishes his first novel, Han d'Islande.
Publishes Cromwell and its famous preface, a landmark text of French Romanticism.
Hernani triggers one of the central literary battles of the Romantic movement.
Publishes Notre-Dame de Paris.
Elected to the Académie française.
His daughter Léopoldine dies, a decisive personal tragedy reflected later in Les Contemplations.
Appointed Peer of France.
Elected to the National Assembly of the Second Republic; gives major speeches on poverty, education, and the death penalty.
Opposes Louis-Napoléon's coup d'état and enters exile.
Publishes Napoléon le Petit.
Publishes Les Châtiments, a major anti-imperial poetic work.
Settles in Guernsey after Jersey; exile becomes a core phase of his writing life.
Publishes Les Contemplations.
Publishes the first series of La Légende des siècles and writes the John Brown letter.
Publishes Les Misérables while in exile.
Publishes Les Travailleurs de la mer.
Publishes L'Homme qui rit.
Returns to France after the fall of the Second Empire.
Briefly serves in the National Assembly; continues public political interventions.
Publishes Quatrevingt-treize.
Becomes senator for Seine.
Publishes L'Art d'être grand-père.
Dies in Paris; receives a state funeral and burial in the Panthéon.
